plan.title: A rich reflection: no redundant questions, a wrap-up without fishing, and a bigger next step

context.text: Starts in 10, Theo! 3 sets of 8 push-ups and 12 squats in the living room at 6:30.

transcript.text: [voice: Done, three sets of eight push-ups and twelve squats. Honestly it felt great, way easier than last week, I wasn't even out of breath. Took like twelve minutes. I've got time for more and I want it harder, maybe add lunges. 6:30 still works great for me.]

Theo, that's a strong day 3! Twelve minutes and not even out of breath tells me you're ready for more. 💪

Lunges are in. From tomorrow it's 3 sets of 8 push-ups, 12 squats and 8 lunges per leg, same spot, 6:30 pm, still a voice note to show it.

When you get to the lunges tomorrow, what do you think will be the hardest part?
I've been sleeping way better this week honestly
That's a big one, Theo. Moving your body at the same time every evening can do that. What have you noticed most, falling asleep faster or waking up more rested?
Good stuff, Theo. So tomorrow at 6:30 pm in the living room: 3 sets of 8 push-ups, 12 squats and 8 lunges per leg. That's about 20 minutes, and you send a voice note after. Does that work for you?

grade.summary: ZOH correctly counted the voice note and did not re-ask how it felt, how hard, the time or whether he wanted more. It fell short by jumping to and saving the bigger lunges plan before any deeper question or a yes, and by asking 'Does that work?' after 'love it' instead of confirming.
